notes: Identified 4 well-recognized candidate roles in gas & liquids transmission / network control. Pipeline Controller merges into existing persona P14 (95% overlap). notes: Midstream compression and pumping stations are operationally anchored by turbomachinery and high-pressure pumping units. Compression Technician is dropped due to predominantly hands-on mechanical wrench work.

Evaluated overlap against existing catalog personas (P01-P33), identifying 2 net-new roles to keep (Gas Plant Operator and Gas Measurement Specialist) and 2 roles to merge into existing personas (Gas Plant Engineer into P26, and Gas Scheduler into P29).

candidates.anchor: ISGOTT 6th Ed. / OCIMF MTMSA Element 8 / SIGTTO / USCG 33 CFR 156 & 127
candidates.anchorCitation: International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals (ISGOTT 6th Edition, Chapters 21 & 26: Cargo Transfer Operations and Ship/Shore Safety Checklist); OCIMF Marine Terminal Management and Self Assessment (MTMSA Element 8); SIGTTO Liquefied Gas Handling Principles on Ships and in Terminals; USCG 33 CFR 156.120 / 33 CFR 127.301.

Calculate cryogenic line cooldown rates, maximum flow ramp-up schedules, and boil-off gas (BOG) return balances based on manifold pressures and tank equilibrium conditions.
Reconcile real-time cargo transfer flow logs, arm operating envelope limits, and manifold pressure trends to produce transfer timesheets, delay records, and demurrage logs.
Generate automated emergency shutdown (ESD-1 and ESD-2) testing sequences and weather abort checklists based on live meteocean forecast data.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Pass — high cognitive, verification, and technical calculation workload. While physical line connection is manual, transfer governance, flow rate modeling, and safety compliance are purely knowledge work.
candidates.oneLine: Manages ship-shore transfer safety, cargo transfer planning, loading arm operations, and operational custody transfer execution during tanker and gas carrier berthing.
candidates.reason: Essential frontline marine transfer governance role recognised internationally across hydrocarbon and LNG berths. Distinct from P15 Terminal Superintendent (who oversees facility P&L, site integrity, staffing, and multi-asset compliance). Governed strictly by ISGOTT, SIGTTO, and OCIMF standards.
candidates.title: Loading Master
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Marine terminal jetty control room, jetty head, ship-shore conference room, and terminal operations center.

candidates.anchor: OCIMF SIRE 2.0 / OCIMF MTMSA / SIGTTO Experience Matrix
candidates.anchorCitation: Oil Companies International Marine Forum (OCIMF) Ship Inspection Report Programme (SIRE 2.0 Governance and Inspection Framework); OCIMF Marine Terminal Management and Self Assessment (MTMSA); SIGTTO LNG Shipping Suggested Competency Standards & Experience Matrix.
exampleAgentableWork: Ingest and evaluate OCIMF SIRE 2.0 negative inspection observations against terminal acceptance criteria to identify and flag critical vessel defect risks.
Verify vessel crew experience matrices against SIGTTO standards (sea time in rank on gas carriers, ship-type experience) prior to issuing marine clearance.
Cross-reference Port State Control (PSC) inspection records, regional memorandum deficiency trends, and Classification Society conditions of class for vetting dossiers.
Audit dynamic mooring analysis studies against OCIMF MEG4 guidelines to verify bollard load safety factors and environmental operating limits at berth.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Pass — purely knowledge- and risk-assessment-driven role with zero manual craft labour. Operates entirely in technical inspection dossiers, compliance frameworks, and clearance protocols.
candidates.oneLine: Assesses maritime safety, vessel structural integrity, operational history, and crew competence to clear or reject tankers, gas carriers, and marine terminals for cargo operations.
candidates.reason: Widely recognised governance discipline across energy charterers, trading arms, and marine terminal operators. Evaluates third-party vessels against strict safety criteria prior to terminal arrival. Entirely distinct from upstream, pipeline, and plant engineering personas.
candidates.title: Marine Assurance Specialist
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Commercial marine desk, regional marine assurance office, or terminal compliance department.

candidates.anchor: API MPMS Chapter 17 / GIIGNL LNG Custody Transfer Handbook / ISO 8943
candidates.anchorCitation: American Petroleum Institute Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards (API MPMS Chapter 17.1 Guidelines for Marine Cargo Inspection, Chapter 17.10.1 Measurement of Cargoes on Board LNG Carriers); GIIGNL LNG Custody Transfer Handbook (7th Edition); ISO 8943 / ISO 6976.
exampleAgentableWork: Calculate net transferred thermal energy (MMBtu) from opening and closing CTMS level soundings, trim/list corrections, and GIIGNL revised Klosek-McKinley density formulas.
Validate gas chromatograph calibration logs and continuous vaporizer sampling records against ISO 10723 and ISO 6976 to verify gross calorific value (GCV) accuracy.
Cross-reconcile vessel custody figures against terminal shore tank radar gauges and fiscal Coriolis meter runs to determine custody transfer discrepancies.
Draft formal Letters of Protest (LOP) and Certificate of Quantity and Quality (COQ) documentation accounting for boil-off gas (BOG) heel deductions and vapor balance.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Pass — intensive calculation, thermodynamic correction, quality audit, and commercial custody reconciliation workload.
candidates.oneLine: Independently measures, audits, and reconciles physical quantities, composition, and thermal energy content of liquid bulk and LNG shipments during custody transfer.
candidates.reason: Recognised globally across liquid bulk shipping and LNG trade. Crucial auditor ensuring transactional accuracy for cargo valued in tens of millions of dollars per lifting. Distinct from P30 Inspection Engineer (mechanical integrity/NDT) and P29 Crude & Product Scheduler.
candidates.title: Cargo Surveyor
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Ship cargo office, marine terminal custody transfer office, quality testing laboratory, and independent inspection agency office.

candidates.anchor: NFPA 59A / ISO 16903 / GPA Midstream
candidates.anchorCitation: National Fire Protection Association (NFPA 59A: Standard for the Production, Storage, and Handling of Liquefied Natural Gas); ISO 16903 (Characteristics of LNG influencing design and material selection); GPA Midstream Technical Standards.
exampleAgentableWork: Simulate mixed-refrigerant loop compositions and compressor power curves in process simulation packages to debottleneck liquefaction capacity.
Analyze boil-off gas (BOG) generation dynamics in cryogenic storage tanks and jetty return lines to balance recondenser and compressor loading.
Model thermal transient stress curves and cool-down temperature differentials for main cryogenic heat exchangers (MCHE) and vacuum-jacketed transfer lines.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Pass — deep engineering analysis and optimization, but substantially duplicative with existing persona P26.
candidates.oneLine: Models, evaluates, and optimizes thermodynamic processes across LNG liquefaction, refrigeration loops, BOG re-liquefaction, and regasification units.
candidates.reason: While operating in cryogenic temperature regimes (-162°C) at marine terminals, the underlying physics, simulation tools, gas treating (acid gas removal, dehydration), compression, refrigeration loops, and process safety tasks overlap >=70% with P26 Gas Plant Engineer. It should be merged into P26 as an LNG/cryogenic domain specialization rather than kept as an independent persona.
candidates.title: LNG Process Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Terminal engineering building, technical services office, or plant operations center.

notes: Evaluated candidate roles across LNG and marine terminals against industry competency standards (OCIMF, SIGTTO, ISGOTT, API MPMS, GIIGNL, NFPA). Retained 3 standalone roles (Loading Master, Marine Assurance Specialist, Cargo Surveyor) and merged 1 adjacent specialism (LNG Process Engineer -> P26 Gas Plant Engineer). Terminal managerial scope remains anchored under existing P15 Terminal Superintendent.

candidates.anchor: API RP 1171 / PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192.12
candidates.anchorCitation: API Recommended Practice 1171 ('Functional Integrity of Natural Gas Storage in Depleted Hydrocarbon Reservoirs and Aquifer Reservoirs', 2nd Edition) and federal safety regulations under 49 CFR § 192.12 mandating underground natural gas storage integrity management programs (SIMP).
exampleAgentableWork: Automating material balance calculations (p/Z surveys) to verify storage pore volume and reconcile working gas versus cushion (base) gas inventory.
Generating multi-well deliverability and pressure-drawdown curves to forecast daily peak withdrawal capacity for pipeline commercial dispatch.
Correlating annual mechanical integrity log data (noise/temperature, casing inspection, and cement evaluation logs) against API RP 1171 threat matrices to prioritize well intervention workovers.
Drafting regulatory compliance reports tracking observation well pressure anomalies and fluid contacts against reservoir containment thresholds.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: High knowledge work suitability: Core responsibilities involve numerical deliverability forecasting, cyclic pressure hysteresis modeling, material balance inventory tracking, and risk assessment for storage integrity management.
candidates.oneLine: Manages underground natural gas storage capacity, inventory reconciliation, cyclic deliverability modeling, and integrity compliance for depleted reservoirs and aquifers.
candidates.reason: While sharing subsurface principles with P06 Reservoir Engineer, the role is uniquely focused on midstream seasonal injection/withdrawal cycling, working-to-cushion gas inventory accounting, pipeline dispatch response, and specialized storage integrity mandates (API RP 1171/PHMSA). Overlap is approximately 35%, justifying a distinct role.
candidates.title: Gas Storage Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Midstream technical engineering offices and underground storage gas control centers, interfacing with field storage compression stations and pipeline dispatchers.

candidates.anchor: API RP 1114 / API RP 1115 / SMRI Guidelines
candidates.anchorCitation: API Recommended Practice 1114 ('Design of Solution-Mined Underground Storage Facilities'), API RP 1115 ('Operation of Solution-Mined Underground Storage Facilities'), API RP 1170 ('Design and Operation of Solution-mined Salt Caverns Used for Natural Gas Storage'), and Solution Mining Research Institute (SMRI) Technical Class Guidelines.
exampleAgentableWork: Evaluating nitrogen-brine interface mechanical integrity test (MIT) pressure trends against API RP 1115 standards to calculate leak rate tolerances and certify cavern tightness.
Processing wireline sonar caliper surveys to generate 3D cavern volume models, detect asymmetrical leaching or roof slabbing, and quantify usable storage volume.
Simulating leaching stages (water injection rates, blanket fluid level control, and brine displacement) to optimize cavern geometry and maintain pillar-to-diameter safety margins.
Modeling cavern thermodynamic response and salt creep convergence under high-frequency injection/withdrawal cycles to update maximum and minimum operating pressure envelopes.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: High knowledge work suitability: Centered on solution mining simulation, wireline sonar caliper interpretation, nitrogen-brine mechanical integrity test calculations, and geomechanical creep modeling.
candidates.oneLine: Designs, leaches, monitors, and validates the structural integrity and thermodynamic performance of solution-mined salt caverns for strategic petroleum reserves and bulk hydrocarbon storage.
candidates.reason: Cavern engineering is a specialized geomechanical and solution-mining discipline governed by distinct standards (API RP 1114/1115/1170, SMRI). It possesses less than 20% overlap with upstream drilling or reservoir engineering personas due to its focus on salt dissolution kinetics, sonar geophysics, and cavity thermodynamics.
candidates.title: Cavern Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Engineering offices, cavern solution mining control facilities, and salt dome storage field sites (including strategic petroleum reserves and commercial NGL/gas storage facilities).

candidates.anchor: API MPMS / AGA Reports
candidates.anchorCitation: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards (MPMS Chapters 2, 3, 5, 11, 12, and 21) and American Gas Association Reports (AGA Nos. 3, 7, 9, 11) governing hydrocarbon measurement, meter proving, tank calibration, volume correction, and electronic flow measurement data integrity.
exampleAgentableWork: Validating meter factor linearity and repeatability from pipe prover and compact prover runs against API MPMS Chapter 12 tolerance criteria.

Reconciling daily bulk terminal gross-to-net volumes using API MPMS Chapter 11 temperature/pressure volume correction factors (CTL/CPL) and tank strapping tables to identify inventory loss/gain anomalies.

Auditing electronic flow measurement (EFM) and gas chromatograph configuration logs against API MPMS Chapter 21.1 / AGA Report No. 9 to detect unlogged orifice plate changes or heating value discrepancies.
Compiling contractual custody transfer discrepancy audit packages with uncertainty analysis for joint venture partners and pipeline shippers.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: High knowledge work suitability: High-intensity analytical, algorithmic, and reconciliatory knowledge work centered on fiscal calculations, meter proving verification, EFM audit trail reviews, and measurement uncertainty budgets.
candidates.oneLine: Ensures accuracy, auditability, and regulatory compliance of fiscal metering, automatic tank gauging, and volume correction calculations across storage facilities and transfer custody points.
candidates.reason: Fiscal measurement and hydrocarbon loss control in bulk storage and pipelines is governed by specialized industry standards (API MPMS, AGA). While P32 Instrument Technician handles physical field hardware calibration and loop checks, the Measurement Engineer owns fiscal algorithms, meter proving validity, uncertainty budgets, and custody reconciliation (overlap ~30%).
candidates.title: Measurement Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Midstream terminal operations centers, central measurement technical offices, and storage facility meter skids / prover loops.

candidates.anchor: API 2350 / API 2610 / NFPA 30
candidates.anchorCitation: API Standard 2350 ('Overfill Protection for Storage Tanks in Petroleum Facilities'), API Standard 2610 ('Design, Construction, Operation, Maintenance, and Inspection of Terminal and Tank Facilities'), and NFPA 30 ('Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code').
exampleAgentableWork: Calculating response times and level alarm setpoints (critical high, automated overfill prevention system trip levels) in compliance with API 2350.
Performing hydraulic pump head and surge pressure calculations for inter-tank transfers and marine jetty loading line-ups.
Evaluating vapor recovery unit (VRU) and thermal oxidizer operating data against environmental permit emission limits during high-rate tank filling.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Moderate knowledge work suitability: Covers hydraulic throughput calculations, tank line-up validation, vapor recovery sizing, and overfill risk assessments.
candidates.oneLine: Provides operational engineering support for bulk liquid tank farm hydraulics, blending systems, vapor control, and overfill prevention systems.
candidates.reason: Approximately 75% of the core responsibilities—hydraulic modeling, pump and piping sizing, manifold design, vapor recovery, and management of change (MOC)—are already encompassed by P12 Facilities Engineer, while terminal operational management is led by P15 Terminal Superintendent. Recommend merging into P12 Facilities Engineer.
candidates.title: Terminal Operations Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Bulk liquid storage terminals, marine oil terminals, and strategic reserve aboveground tank farms.

notes: Storage in midstream spans three primary physical archetypes: underground natural gas storage (depleted reservoirs/aquifers), solution-mined salt caverns (crude oil strategic reserves, NGLs, gas), and aboveground tank terminals. The research identifies three distinct, non-overlapping candidate roles for retention (Gas Storage Engineer, Cavern Engineer, Measurement Engineer), while merging generic terminal surface operations engineering into P12 Facilities Engineer. Purely manual roles (e.g. Tank Farm Operator) are excluded due to lack of agent-preparable knowledge work.
subSegment: Storage (underground gas storage, tank storage, strategic reserves)

candidates.anchor: North American Energy Standards Board (NAESB) / Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)
candidates.anchorCitation: NAESB Wholesale Gas Quadrant (WGQ) Standard 1.3.2 (Nomination Timeline & Cycles), codified in US federal regulation at 18 CFR § 284.12; aligned with ENTSOG Capacity Allocation Mechanisms (Regulation EU 2017/459) and PNGRB Access Code Regulations
exampleAgentableWork: Parsing daily trade capture feeds and customer dispatch notices to assemble nomination schedules aligned with standardized nomination cycle timelines.
Evaluating pipeline Electronic Bulletin Board capacity cut notices during operational constraints and calculating re-routing options across secondary delivery points.
Cross-validating upstream supplier nominations against downstream interconnect confirmations and Maximum Daily Quantity (MDQ) entitlements prior to cycle confirmation deadlines.
Analyzing physical telemetry variances against scheduled flows to prepare intraday re-nomination adjustments and prevent pipeline penalty triggers.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Entirely knowledge work suitable for AI agents: revolves around rule-governed volumetric calculations, multi-leg pipeline pathing logic, interconnect confirmations, and time-critical scheduling under strict regulatory cycle deadlines.
candidates.oneLine: Manages daily and intraday natural gas nominations, confirmations, pipeline capacity bookings, and physical pathing across pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards to match supply with market demand.
candidates.reason: Primary operational commercial role responsible for day-to-day physical gas logistics and capacity scheduling across midstream pipeline networks. Distinct from crude and liquid product schedulers due to compressible gas physics, Electronic Bulletin Board mechanisms, and strict multi-cycle intraday regulatory timelines.
candidates.title: Gas Scheduler
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Midstream commercial operations offices and logistics trading floors, operating pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards (EBBs), energy trading and risk management (ETRM) platforms, and scheduling software portals.

candidates.anchor: North American Energy Standards Board (NAESB) / Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)
candidates.anchorCitation: NAESB WGQ Standard 6.3.1 (Base Contract for Sale and Purchase of Natural Gas) and Quadrant 5 (Capacity Release Standards); FERC 18 CFR Part 284 (Open Access Transportation, Form 549B Index of Customers, and Capacity Release Regulations)
exampleAgentableWork: Ingesting executed transportation, storage, and gathering service agreements to extract commercial terms, capacity rights, and billing parameters into enterprise contract systems.
Evaluating secondary market capacity release postings and incoming bids against tariff bidding windows, creditworthiness thresholds, and recall conditions.
Auditing proposed shipper nomination paths and volume requests against contractual firm capacity entitlements (MDQ/MHQ) and pipeline tariff schedules.
Compiling regulatory compliance reports, such as quarterly index of customer filings and discount rate disclosures, by synthesizing active transportation contract portfolios.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: High agentic potential: heavily focused on structured contract document analysis, tariff interpretation, entitlement verification, capacity release mechanics, and regulatory compliance reporting.
candidates.oneLine: Administers gas transportation, storage, and gathering agreements, enforces tariff compliance, coordinates capacity release bidding, and prepares mandatory regulatory filings.
candidates.reason: Critical commercial and regulatory governance role managing the contractual foundations, capacity rights, and tariff rules that dictate allowable pipeline nominations and revenue terms.
candidates.title: Gas Contract Analyst
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Midstream commercial and contract administration offices, utilizing Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) software, ETRM contract modules, and regulatory filing databases.

candidates.anchor: Council of Petroleum Accountants Societies (COPAS) / NAESB
candidates.anchorCitation: COPAS Accounting Guideline AG-15 (Gas Accounting Manual) & Model Form Gas Balancing Agreements; NAESB WGQ Quadrant 2 (Flowing Gas Standards) and Quadrants 3/4 (Invoicing and Balancing), codified at 18 CFR § 284.12
exampleAgentableWork: Reconciling daily electronic gas measurement meter volume telemetry against scheduled pipeline nominations to compute net shipper imbalances.
Applying pipeline tariff cash-out pricing tiers, index market rates, and penalty multipliers to calculate financial settlements for monthly over-deliveries and under-deliveries.
Administering Operational Balancing Agreement (OBA) accounts between interconnecting midstream operators to track cumulative physical versus scheduled position debts and credits.
Allocating gathering system fuel consumption, processing plant shrinkage, and unaccounted-for gas (UAF) back to individual producer and shipper contracts.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Ideal candidate for AI automation and preparation: tasks are quantitatively rigorous, formula-driven reconciliations of volumetric telemetry against contractual matrices, cash-out schedules, and balancing agreements.
candidates.oneLine: Reconciles physical versus scheduled gas flow variances, administers Operational Balancing Agreements, calculates cash-out settlements, and compiles monthly volumetric allocations.
candidates.reason: Core reconciliation and financial integrity role ensuring that physical molecule movements align with commercial contracts, mitigating imbalance liabilities, and enabling accurate revenue settlement.
candidates.title: Gas Balancing Analyst
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Midstream volumetric accounting and commercial operations offices, leveraging electronic gas measurement (EGM) databases, volumetric allocation engines, and midstream accounting systems.

notes: The midstream commercial sub-segment for capacity booking, nominations, gas contracts, and balancing is organized across three well-defined operational pillars: daily physical scheduling and nominations (Gas Scheduler), contractual capacity entitlement and regulatory tariff governance (Gas Contract Analyst), and volumetric reconciliation, balancing, and settlements (Gas Balancing Analyst). All three roles represent pure knowledge work governed by established industry standards (NAESB, FERC, COPAS, ENTSOG, PNGRB) and have minimal overlap with existing refinery/crude operations roles.
subSegment: Commercial: capacity booking, nominations, gas contracts & balancing

candidates.anchor: American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) / Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) / Institution of Gas Engineers and Managers (IGEM)
candidates.anchorCitation: ASME B31.8 (Gas Transmission and Distribution Piping Systems, Chapter VIII) & PNGRB T4S Regulations (Technical Standards and Specifications including Safety Standards for City Gas Distribution Networks) & IGEM/TD/3 (Steel and PE Pipelines for Gas Distribution)
exampleAgentableWork: Running steady-state hydraulic network simulations to evaluate pressure margins and bottleneck risks for proposed commercial and residential main extensions.

Calculating maximum allowable operating pressure (MAOP), design factor deratings, and required pipe wall thicknesses for steel and medium-density polyethylene (MDPE) mains per ASME B31.8 and local safety codes.
Sizing district regulator stations (DRS), service regulators, and overpressure protection relief valves based on peak winter design-day flow requirements.
Drafting technical design packages, bill of quantities (BOQ), and material requisitions for pipeline reinforcement and relocation projects.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: High cognitive and technical content: performs steady-state and transient hydraulic network simulations, calculates pipe wall thicknesses and pressure drops, evaluates design-day peak capacity under varying heating degree days (HDD), and compiles engineering work packages.
candidates.oneLine: Designs, models, and sizes local natural gas distribution networks, district regulator stations, and customer connections to ensure adequate capacity, pressure, and code compliance.
candidates.reason: Distinct engineering discipline focused on low- and medium-pressure urban gas reticulation, customer load modeling, and city gate/district regulator stations. Unlike P12 (Facilities Engineer) or P13 (Flow Assurance Engineer), this role designs meshed utility distribution networks with plastic/steel piping systems.
candidates.title: Gas Distribution Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Engineering office of a gas utility or local distribution company (LDC), using hydraulic simulation software, GIS platforms, and CAD.

candidates.anchor: U.S. Department of Transportation Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) / Gas Piping Technology Committee (GPTC) / American Gas Association (AGA)
candidates.anchorCitation: 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart P (Gas Distribution Pipeline Integrity Management - DIMP) & ANSI/GPTC Z380.1 (Guide for Gas Transmission, Distribution, and Gathering Piping Systems, Appendix G-192-8)
exampleAgentableWork: Compiling and categorizing historical leak repair records (Grade 1, 2, and 3) to identify spatial clusters and accelerated failure trends across vintage pipe materials.
Executing semi-quantitative risk-ranking models to score distribution mains and service lines based on failure probability, soil characteristics, and proximity to buildings.
Drafting annual DIMP program effectiveness reviews and regulatory compliance reports detailing leak causes, third-party damage rates, and mitigation milestones.
Prioritizing multi-year pipe replacement campaigns targeting legacy cast iron, bare steel, and early-generation plastic (e.g., vintage polymer) piping.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Substantial analytical knowledge work: integrates geographic and operational data to evaluate threats (excavation damage, material degradation, vintage plastics, corrosion), executes relative risk scoring algorithms, and plans long-term capital replacement programs.
candidates.oneLine: Develops and maintains the Distribution Integrity Management Program (DIMP) to identify system threats, rank asset risks, and prioritize remediation across aging distribution mains and services.
candidates.reason: While sharing high-level integrity principles with P27 (Pipeline Integrity Engineer), distribution integrity is fundamentally different. Distribution networks are predominantly unpiggable, low-pressure networks composed of polyethylene and legacy materials where integrity management centers on statistical leak analysis, excavation damage prevention, and DIMP risk ranking under 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart P rather than in-line inspection (ILI/smart pigging) and fracture mechanics under Subpart O.
candidates.title: Distribution Integrity Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Asset management or integrity engineering office at a gas utility, analyzing GIS, work management, and leak history databases.

candidates.anchor: U.S. Department of Transportation PHMSA / American Petroleum Institute (API) / American Gas Association (AGA)
candidates.anchorCitation: 49 CFR Part 192.631 (Control Room Management - CRM) & API RP 1168 (Pipeline Control Room Management)
exampleAgentableWork: Reconciling hourly customer consumption profiles against upstream pipeline gate station nominations to manage system linepack and avoid balancing penalties.
Drafting shift handover logs documenting system abnormalities, active regulator setpoint overrides, odorant injection levels, and pending maintenance isolations.
Synthesizing telemetry trends and low-pressure alarm bursts to formulate immediate network isolation and field response dispatch plans during suspected major main breaks.
Performing daily alarm rationalization reviews to flag nuisance or stale alarms and ensure compliance with Control Room Management (CRM) alarm audit standards.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Real-time supervisory control and operational decision-making: analyzes SCADA telemetry, balances hourly demand against pipeline nominations, coordinates emergency isolations, and logs compliance events under strict control room management rules.
candidates.oneLine: Monitors and operates local distribution network SCADA systems 24/7 to manage linepack, control district regulator pressures, ensure proper odorization, and coordinate leak response dispatches.
candidates.reason: Overlaps >=70% with P14 (Pipeline Controller). Both operate 24/7 SCADA consoles, manage hydraulic alarms, regulate pressures, balance supply and demand, and operate under identical Control Room Management (CRM) statutory requirements (49 CFR 192.631 / API RP 1168). Local distribution nuances (odorization, district regulator stations) can be subsumed into P14.
candidates.title: Gas Controller
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Centralized gas control center / control room of a local gas distribution company.

candidates.anchor: American Gas Association (AGA) / American Petroleum Institute (API) / American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME)
candidates.anchorCitation: AGA Report No. 3 (API 14.3 / Orifice Metering), AGA Report No. 8 (Compressibility Factors of Natural Gas), AGA Report No. 9 (Multipath Ultrasonic Meters), AGA Report No. 11 (Coriolis Meters), and ASME MFC Standards
exampleAgentableWork: Auditing electronic flow computer (EFC) configuration parameters and gas composition inputs against gas chromatograph lab analyses to ensure compliance with AGA Report No. 8 compressibility calculations.
Performing monthly Unaccounted-For Gas (UAG/UFG) volumetric and energy balance reconciliations between city gate custody receipts and aggregated consumer meter billing data.
Sizing ultrasonic, rotary, and Coriolis metering runs and differential pressure transmitters for industrial customer meter and regulation (M&R) stations.
Reviewing meter proving reports, sonic nozzle calibrations, and field transmitter calibration certificates to identify measurement drift and quantify fiscal exposure.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: High analytical and technical rigor: applies fluid thermodynamic equations (supercompressibility, real gas laws), sizes primary and secondary metering elements, validates electronic flow computer calculations, and reconciles system-wide volumetric loss.
candidates.oneLine: Specifies, calibrates, and verifies custody transfer and large customer metering systems, flow computers, and analytical instrumentation to ensure fiscal measurement accuracy and minimize unaccounted-for gas.
candidates.reason: Dedicated technical role focused on thermodynamic custody transfer standards, flow computer algorithms, and fiscal loss (UFG) reconciliation. It does not overlap >=70% with P12 (Facilities Engineer) or P32 (Instrument Technician), as technicians handle physical sensor loop checks and field wiring rather than fluid mechanics, AGA report calculations, and system-wide fiscal reconciliations.
candidates.title: Gas Measurement Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Measurement engineering office and field test benches at gas distribution utilities, working with SCADA, flow computer configuration software, and lab test data.

notes: Analysis covers Gas Distribution Networks (City / Local Distribution Companies - LDCs). Four core roles represent the technical lifecycle: network design & expansion (Gas Distribution Engineer), risk & asset life management (Distribution Integrity Engineer), real-time operations (Gas Controller), and fiscal custody transfer / measurement (Gas Measurement Engineer). Gas Controller is recommended for merge into P14 Pipeline Controller due to >=70% operational and regulatory overlap under Control Room Management (CRM) rules. Purely physical/field trades (e.g., leak survey technicians, plastic pipe fusion joiners, meter installers) were excluded per selection rule 3. All roles are anchored in authoritative standards (ASME, AGA, API, PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192, PNGRB, IGEM) and completely free of company or brand names.

candidates.anchor: OISD-STD-154 / OISD-STD-105
candidates.anchorCitation: OISD-STD-154 ('Safety Aspects in Functional Training') mandates competency standards and safety qualifications for supervisory personnel directing continuous refinery processing units, shift handover discipline, and emergency isolation; complemented by OISD-STD-105 ('Work Permit System') for authorizing high-risk permits-to-work.
exampleAgentableWork: Reconciling end-of-shift DCS operational logs, unit throughput tallies, and chemical injection rates against daily production targets and shift handover notes.
Cross-checking active and pending Permit-to-Work (PTW) applications across primary and secondary units to detect SIMOPS conflicts, blind list mismatches, and overlapping isolation boundaries.
Drafting preliminary shift incident and near-miss event logs following unexpected unit upsets, relief valve lifts, or flaring excursions against Safe Operating Limit (SOL) baselines.
Generating shift equipment status exception briefs prior to shift exchange, flagging bypassed safety interlocks, tagged-out relief valves, and unspared critical machinery.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: High; substantial cognitive work in operational logbook reconciliation, Safe Operating Limit (SOL) excursion analysis, PTW simultaneous operations (SIMOPS) deconfliction, and shift handover discrepancy reviews.
candidates.oneLine: Directs 24/7 operating crews across primary and secondary process units, governing safe operating envelopes, permit-to-work authorizations, emergency responses, and shift-to-shift handovers.
candidates.reason: Essential frontline operating authority on rotating shifts. Overlaps only partially (~35%) with P03 Board Operator (console execution only) and P16 Refinery Process Engineer (daytime long-term technical optimization), filling a critical shift leadership gap.
candidates.title: Shift Supervisor
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Central Control Room (CCR) supervisory console, plant operational briefing room, and unit shift handover stations.

candidates.anchor: ANSI/ISA-18.2 / ISA-106
candidates.anchorCitation: ANSI/ISA-18.2 ('Management of Alarm Systems for the Process Industries') and ISA-106 ('Procedure Automation for Continuous Process Operations') specify engineering lifecycle standards, alarm rationalization requirements, and advanced regulatory control architectures for continuous refining process units.
exampleAgentableWork: Screening regulatory PID control loops across crude distillation and hydroprocessing units to detect oscillating, saturated, or sticking valves requiring tuning or maintenance.
Analyzing alarm flood records and standing alarm frequencies against ANSI/ISA-18.2 KPI benchmarks to prepare alarm rationalization change recommendations.
Evaluating multivariable predictive controller (MPC) constraint matrices and model gains against historical unit operating data to prepare step-testing protocol briefs.
Drafting Management of Change (MOC) technical impact assessments for proposed control logic revisions, trip setpoint modifications, or automated procedural state sequences.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: High; highly digital and analytical knowledge work encompassing loop performance diagnostics, MPC matrix tuning, step-test analysis, and alarm flood rationalization.
candidates.oneLine: Designs, tunes, and sustains multivariable predictive control (MPC/APC) applications, regulatory control loops, and alarm management systems across complex primary and secondary conversion units.
candidates.reason: Distinct technical specialization responsible for dynamic control layers and APC/MPC performance. Overlaps partially (~45%) with P16 Refinery Process Engineer (who focuses on steady-state chemistry, catalysts, and yields) and P32 Instrument Technician (who manages field hardware), making it a viable standalone candidate.
candidates.title: Process Control Engineer
candidates.whereTheWorkHappens: Central control room engineering workstations, plant technical services engineering offices, and DCS/APC simulation consoles.

candidates.anchor: OPITO Global Vocational Qualification 3: Downstream Processing
candidates.anchorCitation: OPITO Global Vocational Qualification 3: Oil and Gas Processing Operations (Hydrocarbons - Downstream) defines competency units for plant equipment monitoring, line-up verifications, and physical isolation of hydrocarbon processing facilities.
exampleAgentableWork: Compiling field gauge readings and manual round observations against historical baseline ranges to highlight equipment anomalies.
Cross-referencing lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) energy isolation check sheets against P&IDs and blind list drawings before maintenance turnover.
Drafting standard pre-startup field alignment checklists following pump or heat exchanger turnaround maintenance.
candidates.knowledgeWorkVerdict: Low; work is predominantly hands-on physical execution within battery limits, with minor documentation and checklist execution.
